steps.message:
FILES: rich/table.py:452
ROOT CAUSE: When `add_row` creates new columns because the number of renderables exceeds the current number of columns, it instantiates `Column` without specifying the `highlight` property. This causes the new columns to use the `Column.highlight` default of `False` instead of inheriting the `Table.highlight` value.
CHANGE: Modify the `Column` instantiation in `add_row` from `column = Column(_index=index)` to `column = Column(_index=index, highlight=self.highlight)`.
TEST: tests/test_table.py (A new test case should be added to verify that columns added via `add_row` inherit the `Table.highlight` property).

I updated `rich/table.py` in the `add_row` method to ensure that columns created dynamically when the number of renderables exceeds the current column count inherit the `Table.highlight` value instead of defaulting to `False`.

Changed `Column(_index=index)` to `Column(_index=index, highlight=self.highlight)`.

To verify, you can run `pytest tests/test_table.py`.
